The app writes every day it reads into its own table and fetched what Health Connect still had on first launch. If nothing was there, it fills up from now on — one day per day.

%1$d days stored, since %2$s. Today does not count — a day in progress always has too little, and today\'s weekday would otherwise always be the weakest. A weekday stays empty until it has been recorded %3$d times.

Light bar: total sleep, dark the deep sleep. Dashed your average, coloured your ideal.
The midpoint of your nights over %1$d days.
Counted from 6 pm so that midnight is no edge: 23:10 and 00:30 are eighty minutes apart, but as clock times almost a whole day.
From the daily low to the daily high; the light line is the resting heart rate.
All heart rate readings of the last 14 days, laid over each other by time of day. The line is the moving median — this is how a day normally goes for you.
Nothing from SupCycle yet. The watch reports its state as soon as something is ticked off there — there is nothing to fetch retroactively.

%1$s — appear from %2$d days in common. Any line can be drawn through a handful of points, and it would look convincing.

Correlation is not causation. Someone who sleeps long may have a lower resting heart rate — or someone with a lower resting heart rate sleeps better, or both depend on a third thing that is not shown here at all.

The same settings as on the config page in the Pebble app. Change them here or there; what the watch reported last is what counts.
The target applies immediately and resets today\'s goal; “Goal+” on the watch raises it for today only.
Long press: in steps of five. The zones here use the same value.
Within this window the watch records movement and heart rate every minute and HRV every half hour. In the morning this app works out the sleep from it.
Names at most 15 bytes — accented letters count double. “Cycle running for” says which week of the course you are in; the watch then shows the right phase straight away.
Without Health Connect there is nothing to read. The app then logs nothing either; navigation to the watch still works.
Steps over the day, every half hour
Faded behind is the average of the last two weeks. That shows whether movement is missing or just has not happened yet: in the morning every curve is low.
No phases logged — the record only knows the duration of this night.

The line is your ideal of %1$s, adjustable behind the gear. What lies above is shown in its own colour. Last night is missing here: it is already shown above, and in the chart it would stand next to seven finished ones.
Each dot is a reading, the line the moving median, dashed the resting heart rate. The day boundary is a counting boundary, not a screen — otherwise last night\'s curve would not be visible.
The ± is the spread of heart rate values over the night — how calm it was. It is NOT the HRV: that measures the variation between consecutive beats, and for that you need their timing, not whole bpm.
The resting heart rate is estimated (≈)
Nobody logged one. Shown is the average of the ten lowest readings of the night — close, but not the same. If the watch logs one itself, the sign disappears.

A dash means: nothing is there — not that the value is zero. Steps, heart rate and sleep must come from the watch or other apps. The rating from 1 to 5 stays here: the record has no entry type for “how I feel”. What is really there is shown in the settings.
1 means exhausted, 5 means fresh. One number a day, and in three weeks you see what it depends on.
Without Health Connect there is nothing to read and nothing to log.
Everything goes into the health record

This app logs water, caffeine and supplements there itself — so they are available to other apps too and survive a reinstall. Water is reported by Drinktervall from the watch, supplements by SupCycle. Every entry carries a latch against duplicates.
What is in the blood, and ☾ at bedtime

Every cup is a jump followed by a slow decline: the body breaks down caffeine with a half-life of about five hours. An espresso at 5 pm is still half there at 10 pm. The five hours are an average — they vary between about three and seven —, the curve shows the shape, not a measurement. The bedtime is last night\'s.
Coffee 80 mg, espresso 60, tea 40, energy drink 80

Ballpark figures for a usual serving — ten milligrams make no difference. For the question “caffeine after 4 pm versus deep sleep” it is the timing that matters most anyway, and the app remembers that itself. Everything also goes into the health record.
Today, glass by glass — the bigger the drop, the more

Drinktervall reports every glass from the watch, with its time. The goal is eight glasses of 3 dl unless Drinktervall sends another — a ballpark figure, not a rule. Today counts, unlike steps and sleep: half a day of water is not a weak day, but the state you reach for.
Nothing from SupCycle yet. The watch reports its state as soon as something is ticked off there — there is nothing to fetch retroactively, it starts with the first dose.
SupCycle knows what is due today.
Seven days: light planned, dark taken

The taken part sits INSIDE the planned one. Two bars side by side would leave open whether “3 taken” was out of three or out of eight. SupCycle knows what is due today; here only what was ticked off is shown.

As soon as you finish one on the watch, it appears here — with the route if the phone was with you. Without Kieselsport on the watch this screen stays empty; workouts from other apps appear as soon as they are in the health record.

The last three months, by time
Four weeks. The colour is the type, the size the duration; a ring outside means a second type was added.

The heart rate variability from this session, measured by the watch. Higher means more relaxed; it is comparable with the night values from Kieselsport.

Length by length — red the fast ones, blue the slow ones. The axis counts lengths, not minutes.

enable in OsmAnd: Menu › Plugins › Kiesel-Helper
Receives what the watch reports, and fetches from OsmAnd what belongs on the watch for navigation.
What you tap in the app is logged as a nutrition entry with the amount of caffeine. The record is the source here too: what is read is what is there, not the app\'s own count.
Every glass you drink is logged as an amount of water, with the time from the watch. The same glass only once.
Today\'s goal as the watch last reported it — with “Goal+” it can be above the target.

At night Kieselsport records movement and heart rate every minute and measures HRV every half hour. In the morning Kiesel-Helper works out the sleep from it — asleep, woken, deep, REM and light sleep — and logs it together with resting heart rate and night HRV. A single HRV measurement from the watch menu is logged as well. The night window is set under Workout → Kieselsport.

What is due today, what of it is ticked off, and the names. Every supplement taken goes into the record as a nutrition entry — without amounts, because SupCycle knows names and cycles, not milligrams.

A finished workout is logged as an exercise session, with sets or lengths, the heart rate curve and — for running, bike, hiking — the route from the phone. Steps, distance and calories are logged by the Pebble app itself.
Turn type, distance, street and arrival time go to the watch — from OsmAnd\'s own interface, not from its notification.
“System” follows the phone\'s night switch. The widget follows the choice here from Android 12; before that it follows the system.
Background, cards, text and the colours of the three tabs come from the wallpaper. Sports, sleep phases, heart rate zones, water and caffeine keep their colours — they carry meaning.
Material You is available from Android 12.
It appears as a coloured line in the sleep chart and in the weekly profile — and the trend counts in how many nights you reached it.
Applies to everything that means “today”. Sleep has its own window: a night starts at 6 pm, regardless of when the day starts.
Paste a link and check it. Skips Android\'s link approval — what works here but not outside is down to it.
“Show place” puts the point on the map and leaves the start to you. Navigation that starts by itself otherwise also decides whether you drive at all right now.
OsmAnd refused (%1$s). Usually the permission is missing there under Menu → Plugins.
Only while in use — not enough

The watch has no GPS. During a workout the phone records the route — with a visible notification in the bar, and only between start and stop. Without the permission the workout is still logged, just without a map.

“Only while using the app” is not enough here. The workout starts on the watch while the phone is in your pocket and this app is closed — in that state Android allows no location, and the route would stay empty. “Allow all the time” is needed. Location is still only measured between start and stop of a workout.
Fills the trend from what Health Connect has stored

Without further permission Health Connect only releases the thirty days before the first permission — after a reinstall, one month. With the permission for older data the app fetches a year. What is only in the app — the day\'s rating, the supplements — stays untouched. Not every phone knows this permission; then it stays at one month.
Nothing found. Is the read permission missing?

resources.string: Daily table and routes into a folder on the phone

The health record keeps about thirty days. Everything this app calculates in weekly profiles and correlations is then only in its own table — and that lives in the app data of a single phone. It is saved as readable JSON: that is still worth something even if this app no longer exists. The routes lie next to it, one file per workout, and are uploaded only once.
Folder on the phone no longer reachable
No folder chosen on the phone
Choose a folder that a sync app keeps in sync

In the dialog, choose a folder that DAVx5, Nextcloud, mailbox.org Drive or Syncthing synchronises — or a folder in “Documents”. Kiesel-Helper writes there, the sync app uploads it; login and server quirks are its business. Without a sync app it stays a copy on the phone that can be collected. It is saved as readable JSON.
Restoring only adds what is missing here — existing days and routes stay as they are. Continue?
Without Health Connect nothing can be logged. Navigation to the watch still works.
Without it a measurement arrives and disappears silently — you only notice when you look for it.
What is in the record (48 h)
An empty field on the health screen has its answer here: if nothing is in the record, nobody is writing it.

OsmAnd only lets other apps in after a switch. Kiesel-Helper is already in the list there — the first connection attempt added it, just switched off. After flipping it, come back here, that is enough.
Without a connection to OsmAnd, Kieselstrasse stays empty on the watch. OsmAnd must be installed; the connection is made as soon as this service runs.
%1$d nights stored, the newest from %2$s. Export it as CSV to compare with another sleep tracker, or re-analyse it after an update.
